paper.title: ULTRA: Unified Multimodal Control for Autonomous Humanoid Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation

review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: Unified multimodal humanoid controller spanning dense reference tracking and sparse perception-conditioned goal following.

sections_read.purpose: Identify reliance on dense predefined reference motions.
Inspect physics-driven retargeting, privileged teacher and multimodal student.
Verify hardware tracking and sparse-goal results.
Record perception, MoCap and command limits.

research_question: Can one humanoid controller combine dense motion tracking with sparse goals and realistic egocentric sensing?
contributions: Physics-driven neural retargeting and a distilled multimodal controller with RL fine-tuning.

method.summary: A privileged dense-tracking teacher is distilled into a latent multimodal student; PPO fine-tuning expands goal-conditioned behavior from point clouds, poses or sparse transforms.
assumptions: Human-object motion can be retargeted into physically feasible robot trajectories.
Sparse object geometry can be extracted from depth or supplied by MoCap.

study_context.sample_or_scale: Large-scale simulation training; real dense tracking over 26 trials and sparse goal following over 10 trials per direction/mode.

evaluation.design: Retargeting and tracking baselines are compared in simulation; MuJoCo OOD tests and real MoCap/egocentric deployments assess transfer.

findings.finding: Sparse goal following transferred to hardware, but onboard depth perception lagged external motion capture.
findings.scope: Reported object-transport tasks on one Unitree G1.

author_stated.limitation: Severe point-cloud occlusion, MoCap marker occlusion and aggressive or infeasible user goals can cause failure.

reader_inferred.boundary: The system advances beyond reference replay but still uses operator-specified object transforms rather than high-level task planning.
reader_inferred.basis: Sparse future object transforms are issued through keyboard commands in the real deployment.

transfer_boundary: Supports goal-conditioned whole-body control with structured object goals; language-level autonomy and robust open-world perception remain separate.

design_strengths: Unifies dense and sparse control modes.
Reports onboard egocentric and external-state hardware results separately.
design_risks: Simple dominant-cluster depth segmentation limits perception complexity.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: Simulation baselines share retargeting/tracking tasks; sparse goal following lacks equivalent tracking-only baselines by construction.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Success captures stability and goal achievement, while low trial counts limit precision.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: Architecture, randomization and training stages are detailed.

evidence_cards.claim: On real G1 sparse-goal following, MoCap object state achieved 80% vertical and 90% lateral success, while egocentric depth achieved 50% and 60%, respectively.
evidence_cards.relation: Supports perception-conditioned whole-body control while quantifying the current onboard-perception penalty.
evidence_cards.summary: The real-world table separates external-state and onboard egocentric control modes.
evidence_cards.source_context: TABLE IV : Real-world success rates on the OMOMO subset using a Unitree G1 humanoid. Each task is evaluated over two trials. MoCap provides object pose tracking for non-egocentric control modes, while the egocentric setting relies only on onboard sensing. MoCap is used for success evaluation in all settings. Dense reference tracking is direction-agnostic and thus reported as a single success rate.
